text:
Alex: Heads up — NA-west GPU pool showing sustained pressure (92% 12h avg, queue length +120). Thinking we do a staged regional drain to NA-east/NA-central. Want to avoid breaking pinned sessions for enterprise tenants. Thoughts?
Priya: Can you drop the graphs? Which fleets are hot?
Alex: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/gpu-fleet?orgId=1 — regional GPU util, queue growth. Hot pools: na-west-gpu-pool-3 and -5. Also seeing increased OOMs on small V100 instances.
Jin: +1 staged shift. Proposal: shift 10% every 3m with health-check gates. If 5xx rate > 0.5% or p95 latency > 200ms during a window, pause and rollback one step. Also enable conn-drain TTL=30s.
Casey: Important: enterprise customers (ids: corp-acme, corp-beta) have session-affinity pinned via X-Redwood-Customer header. We should exclude them from weight changes or warm their KV caches before moving.
Morgan: KV cache cold-start will tank latency for some embed-heavy tenants. I can prewarm top 5 tenants via a small warm-up job — usage: 
`````
# warm kv cache for tenant
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $WARMY" \
  -X POST https://internal-api/redwood/warm_kv \
  -d '{"tenant":"corp-acme","keys":5000}'
`````
Do we want that for all excluded customers or just 2?
Priya: Do warm for corp-acme and corp-beta, and for corp-gamma if time.
SRE-OnCall: Watch egress cost — shifting 30% cross-region will spike inter-region bandwidth. Recommend cap initial shift to 20% and monitor egress bytes/second.
Alex: Ok plan updated: 20% initial shift, then +10% every 4m if health gates pass. I'll run redwoodctl to apply staged change.
Alex: Running: 
`````
redwoodctl gslb set-weights --region na-west -20 --region na-east +10 --region na-central +10 --staged --step 10 --interval 240 --health-gate "p95_latency<200,5xx_rate<0.5%" --exclude-tenants corp-acme,corp-beta
`````
ops-bot: gslb-change-initiated: id=chg-20240301-77 by Alex — staging enabled
gslb-bot: step-1 applied: na-west (-20) na-east (+10) na-central (+10) — new weights committed. Monitoring health metrics.
Morgan: Warm jobs kicked for corp-acme and corp-beta — ETA 2m.
Jin: Gate check window passing so far. p95=140ms, 5xx=0.12%. Proceeding to schedule next step.
gslb-bot: step-2 scheduled in 240s
Casey: Noted slight increase in auth latency for corp-gamma but it's within gate. Keep an eye on retries from SDKs.
Alex: step-2 applied — na-west (-30 total) na-east (+15) na-central (+15)
gslb-bot: alert: na-east p95 spiked to 340ms for a 30s window — triggering pause and rollback 1 step
Alex: rolling back one step now to previous weights
ops-bot: gslb-rollback-completed: reverted to step-1 weights. Incident created: INC-20240301-9 — assigned to eng-infra
SRE-OnCall: Good catch — looks like na-east microburst on a specific cluster (na-east-gpu-pool-12). Please divert more to na-central while pool is investigated.
Jin: Adjusting plan: increase na-central by additional 5% (to soak) and keep na-east at step-1. Running redwoodctl quick-adjust for na-central.
Alex: quick adjust executed: na-central +5. Monitoring.
Priya: Can we also open a ticket with infra to repro the microburst? Link to the incident ticket once created.
Casey: Noting cost TL: initial egress estimate for total planned shift would be ~1.2TB/hr -> ~$900/hr. With rollback + soak we should be ok for now but track.
Alex: Thanks team. Standby for infra postmortem. I'll update INC-20240301-9 with timeline and actions.
SRE-OnCall: marking thread resolved for now; keep message updates in the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
